The crown in the school bag

On Thursday, our class made tall paper crowns for a play. I thought it was the ____1____ crown in the room. Then the bell rang, and I had to put it into my school ____2____. The top was too high. I pushed it down and heard the paper ____3____.

At home, I took it out carefully. One star hung from a small piece of paper. I felt ____4____ because the play was the next morning. He wanted to wear the crown, but I told him not to ____5____ it. 

Dad gave me some paper and glue. "You can make the back stronger," he said. I cut a short strip and put it ____6____ the broken star. We left the crown on a shelf while the glue ____7____. 

After dinner, the star stood up again. I let my brother try the crown for a ____8____. Then I took it back. I did not want another ____9____ before morning.

This time, Dad found a wide box. The crown could stand inside without bending. I wrote my name on the ____10____, closed it and put it beside the door. At school, I carried the box with both hands. My friends wanted to know what was ____11____. 

During the play, the tallest star moved a little when I turned my ____12____. After the final song, I took the crown off and looked at the repair. Nobody in the audience had seen the strip of paper at the ____13____. I was glad Dad had helped me make it strong, not just pretty. On the way home, the crown travelled in its box again. My bag was useful for books, but it was the ____14____ place for a tall paper crown. I had learned that before I had to make the whole thing ____15____.
